CFML Language Reference: Tags

CFX Tags (CFX_HELLO, CFX_DICE, CFX_SYSINFO)

CFX tags are custom tags written in C or C++ and compiled into a shared library. They are registered on the CFX Tags page of the Administrator and then called like any other tag, with a name starting with CFX_. KoldFusion ships three samples (sources in the cfx directory of the distribution): CFX_HELLO writes a greeting, CFX_DICE rolls dice, and CFX_SYSINFO returns a query describing the server machine.

Category

Extensibility

Syntax

<CFX_HELLO NAME="name"
    VARIABLE="variable_name"
    DEBUG>

<CFX_DICE ROLLS="number"
    SIDES="number"
    VARIABLE="variable_name">

<CFX_SYSINFO NAME="query_name">

Attributes

NAME (CFX_HELLO)
Optional, default "World". Who to greet. The greeting is written to the page unless VARIABLE is given.
VARIABLE (CFX_HELLO)
Optional. Variable that receives the greeting instead of the page.
DEBUG (CFX_HELLO)
Optional. When present, the tag also writes a line of debug output after the greeting.
ROLLS (CFX_DICE)
Optional, default "2". Number of dice to roll, 1 to 100.
SIDES (CFX_DICE)
Optional, default "6". Sides per die, 2 to 1000.
VARIABLE (CFX_DICE)
Optional. Variable that receives the total. The rolls (for example "3 + 5 = 8") are always written to the page.
NAME (CFX_SYSINFO)
Required. Name of the query to create, with the columns Item and Value: operating system, release, machine, host name, uptime, load average, memory, processors and a note.

Usage

A CFX tag sees its attributes, can write to the page, set variables in the calling page, read a query passed in a QUERY attribute, create new queries and raise errors, which reach your page as type Application and can be caught with CFTRY. Calling an unregistered CFX tag raises "The CFX custom tag ... was not found in the custom tag database".

To write your own, include kfx.h and export a function ProcessTagRequest(CFXRequest *request); the request offers AttributeExists, GetAttribute, GetAttributeList, GetQuery, Write, SetVariable, AddQuery, Debug, WriteDebug and ThrowException, much like the CFX API of ColdFusion. Build it as a .so file, put it in the cfx directory and register it in the Administrator. Java CFX tags need a JVM, which KoldFusion does not configure. For tags written in CFML, see CFMODULE.

Example

Opens the example in a new window. The example runs on this server, so it only works when you browse from the server itself (127.0.0.1).
<P><B>CFX_HELLO</B>: <CFX_HELLO NAME="Netscape Navigator user"></P>
<CFX_HELLO NAME="Ada" VARIABLE="Greeting">
<CFOUTPUT><P>Stored in a variable: <I>#Greeting#</I></P></CFOUTPUT>

<P><B>CFX_DICE</B>: <CFX_DICE ROLLS="3" SIDES="6" VARIABLE="Total"></P>
<CFOUTPUT><P>The total, from VARIABLE: #Total#<CFIF Total GTE 15> (jackpot!)</CFIF></P></CFOUTPUT>
<CFTRY>
  <CFX_DICE ROLLS="0">
  <CFCATCH TYPE="Application"><CFOUTPUT><P>Zero dice: #CFCATCH.Message#</P></CFOUTPUT></CFCATCH>
</CFTRY>

<P><B>CFX_SYSINFO</B>:</P>
<CFX_SYSINFO NAME="Sys">
<TABLE BORDER=1 CELLPADDING=3>
<CFOUTPUT QUERY="Sys"><TR><TD>#Item#</TD><TD>#Value#</TD></TR></CFOUTPUT>
</TABLE>
